Battery drain on our MT6989-based wearable increased from 12 mA to 38 mA at idle after enabling an always-on 1 fps camera preview feature. The power regression is far larger than expected from the sensor power spec (OV2740: 8 mA active). PMIC current log and DRAM state log:

  $ cat /sys/class/power_supply/battery/current_now
  -38200  (uA, negative = discharge)

  $ cat /sys/kernel/debug/ddr/self_refresh_state
  not_in_self_refresh  (expected: self_refresh)

  [  idle path] mtk-isp: pipe_0: streaming at 1fps, DMA active
  [  idle path] ddr: self_refresh_blocked_by: ISP_DMA (reason: outstanding_transaction)

The LPDDR5 is not entering self-refresh because the ISP DMA engine holds an outstanding transaction at all times, even between frames at 1 fps. LPDDR5 in active mode consumes approximately 25 mA more than in self-refresh on our JEDEC JESD79-5 characterization. How should the ISP DMA be gated between frames to allow LPDDR5 self-refresh entry, and what latency budget is acceptable for the DMA wake-up on the next 1 fps trigger?
